item.text: {"analysis":"Trial succeeded with host validation macro HR@10 of 0.505, matching the stated baseline. Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.560, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.545, Electronics 0.375, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.540. Against the supplied baseline category references, changes were −0.020, +0.005, −0.045, and +0.060 respectively. Uniform transition weighting produced no aggregate improvement; category gains offset regressions. These results do not establish that weighting caused the differences. The proposed 0.005–0.015 gain was not observed. Host validation is authoritative; historical comparison constants embedded in the script do not describe this trial’s measured results.","code_summary":"Trains one independent SASRec model per category from scratch with seed 42 and loads one selected checkpoint per category. Each model uses 96-dimensional embeddings, two causal Transformer blocks, two attention heads, dropout 0.2, and jointly trained causal history attention pooling with a learned gate. Scores use normalized embeddings, learned temperature, and item bias. Training uses sampled-softmax cross-entropy with 256 unique uniform batch negatives and complete-training-history exclusion. At most 24 valid transitions are selected per history, weighted uniformly and averaged within each history before averaging across eligible histories. Prefix augmentation, AdamW, cosine learning-rate decay, validation-based checkpoint selection, and dataset routing remain intact. The generated predictor reconstructs the same architecture without ensembles or separately fitted scorers."}
